newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania cotton buying starts, output down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania cotton buying starts, output down sharply.

text.p: Tanzania has begun its annual cotton buying season, but availability is seen sharply lower because of drought, a senior cotton board official said on Wednesday.
Thomas Fille, marketing manager for the state-run Tanzania Cotton Seed and Lint Board (TCLSB), told Reuters that the buying season was expected to last three months.
"The crop this year -- we expect around 300,000 to 330,000 bales. This crop has been effected by the drought," said Fille. The total compared with output of 473,000 bales in 1995/96.
Annual export earnings would fall to around $80 million in 1996/97 from $109 million in 1995/96, Fille said.
Tanzanian cotton is highly regarded for its quality.
The crop, grown mainly around the shores of Lake Victoria, is totally dependent on seasonal rain as irrigation is non-existent.
Domestic use has fallen from a peak of 100,000 bales in the 1980s to a current level of 30,000 bales, industry officials say.
Following the move to free market policies in the late 1980s, textile output in Tanzania has virtually stopped with only two out of 37 mills in operation.
The country's main cotton markets are Europe, which accounts for 30 percent, with Malaysia, Singapore and Taiwan taking the rest.
